:::{#exm-ols-mean-cov}
#### Covariance matrix of $\evb$ for the `birthweight` model

For the `birthweight` model with an interaction term (`bw_lm2`),
@thm-ols-mean-cov says that
$\Cov{\evb \mid \mX} = \ss \inv{\tp{\mX}\mX}$.
Replacing the unknown $\ss$ by its estimate $\es^2$
gives the estimated covariance matrix that `vcov()` reports:

```{r}
#| label: bw-vcov-by-hand
#| code-fold: show
bw_x <- model.matrix(bw_lm2)
bw_vcov_by_hand <- sigma(bw_lm2)^2 * solve(crossprod(bw_x))
max(abs(bw_vcov_by_hand - vcov(bw_lm2)))
```

The largest difference between the two matrices is zero,
up to floating-point rounding error.

To see that $\evb$ is unbiased with this covariance matrix,
we can treat the fitted coefficients and $\es$ as the true $\vb$ and $\s$,
simulate many new outcome vectors $\vY$ with the same design matrix $\mX$,
and refit the model to each one:

```{r}
#| label: bw-ols-sim
#| code-fold: show
set.seed(1)
bw_beta <- coef(bw_lm2)
bw_mu <- drop(bw_x %*% bw_beta)
bw_sims <- replicate(10000, {
  bw_y <- rnorm(length(bw_mu), mean = bw_mu, sd = sigma(bw_lm2))
  drop(solve(crossprod(bw_x), crossprod(bw_x, bw_y)))
})
rbind(
  true = bw_beta,
  mean_of_estimates = rowMeans(bw_sims),
  formula_se = sqrt(diag(bw_vcov_by_hand)),
  sd_of_estimates = apply(bw_sims, 1, sd)
)
```

The average of the 10,000 simulated estimates is close to $\vb$ for every coefficient,
and the standard deviation of the simulated estimates is close to
the standard error from $\ss \inv{\tp{\mX}\mX}$,
as @eq-ols-mean-cov predicts.
:::
